summary: the decay time and the amplitude of a single exponential decay fitted by least squares on the logarithm over a window the caller names

inputs.name: points
inputs.meaning: pairs [t, y] of a decaying signal, the time and the value each in one unit throughout

inputs.name: window
inputs.meaning: [t_first, t_last], the times between which (both included) the points are fitted, in the unit of the points' times

outputs.name: decay_time
outputs.meaning: tau of y = A exp(-t/tau), minus one over the fitted slope of ln y against t, in the unit of the points' times; null when not fitted or when the fitted slope is not negative

outputs.name: amplitude
outputs.meaning: A, the fitted value at t = 0, in the unit of the points' values

outputs.name: residual_standard_deviation
outputs.meaning: of ln y about the fitted line, the residual sum of squares over n - 2, rooted; null with two points

outputs.name: points_fitted
outputs.meaning: how many points lay in the window

outputs.name: why
outputs.meaning: why nothing was fitted; absent when fitted

validity: a single exponential over the window; least squares on ln y weighs every point's relative error alike, so noise near zero, where ln y is wide, pulls the fit, and the window is the caller's to keep it out; a sum of exponentials gives an effective decay time that depends on the window

source.citation: Morozov and Spagnolie (2015), Introduction to Complex Fluids, chapter 1 of Complex Fluids in Biological Systems (read 2026-11-21, https://people.math.wisc.edu/~spagnolie/Papers/Introduction_to_Complex_Fluids.pdf; mat-20261121-morozov-spagnolie-2015-complex-fluids); NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Section 4.4.3.1 Least Squares (read 2026-11-17, https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmd/section4/pmd431.htm; meta_agent/inbox/materials/20261117-nist-sematech-least-squares)
source.locus: Morozov and Spagnolie, equation (1.51): the stress of a Maxwell fluid after a step relaxes as exp(-t/lambda), lambda = eta/G, so its relaxation modulus is G exp(-t/lambda); NIST/SEMATECH 4.4.3.1: least squares chooses the parameters that minimise the sum of squared deviations, a model linear in its parameters (here ln y = ln A - t/tau) solved directly, the residual standard deviation that sum over n - p, rooted

note: Written for meta_agent/tasks/034, where the relaxation time of an Oldroyd-B fluid of Hookean dumbbells is read from the relaxation modulus of an equilibrium Brownian-dynamics run (shear_relaxation_modulus_green_kubo). No value of either source stands behind the worked cases: each is an exact exponential worked by hand, on two unrelated kinds of system. v2 (tasks/034, failure bd-2): a value that is not a finite number is refused with a why, where v1 carried it into its output; seen when HOOMD-blue's pressure tensor, read on steps it had not computed, came back as not-a-number and v1 of exponential_decay_fit said fitted.
